name: vscode-isabelle
description: Isabelle proof assistant support for unmodified VS Code, on top of Isabelle's own language server.

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Isabelle/PIDE
walkthroughs.description: Set up Isabelle in VS Code and prove your first lemma.

steps.title: Connect Isabelle2025-2
steps.description:
The extension runs your Isabelle2025-2 distribution; the VSCodium bundled with it is not needed. It is found automatically in the usual places.
[Check Isabelle](command:isabelle.checkInstallation)
[Download Isabelle](https://isabelle.in.tum.de/)

steps.title: Install the Isabelle fonts
steps.description:
Symbols like these need Isabelle's fonts; ordinary fonts show boxes. Install every file in the font folder (Windows: right-click, Install; macOS: Font Book; Linux: copy to ~/.local/share/fonts, run fc-cache -f), then restart VS Code.
[Open Font Folder](command:isabelle.revealFonts)
[Use Them for Theories](command:isabelle.useIsabelleFont)

media.altText: Isabelle symbols such as script letters, bold digits and long arrows, drawn in the Isabelle font

steps.title: Turn on the extended server
steps.description:
Recommended. Adds Find Theorems, indentation, more colours and more panels. Your Isabelle installation is not changed.
[Turn It On](command:toSide:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22isabelle.extendedServer%22%5D)

steps.title: Restart VS Code
steps.description:
Restart VS Code after installing the Isabelle fonts or changing the extended server setting.
[Reload VS Code](command:workbench.action.reloadWindow)

steps.title: Open the tutorial
steps.description:
A short theory to try everything on. Isabelle checks it around the cursor as you read and type.
[Open Tutorial](command:isabelle.openTutorial)

steps.title: Type mathematics
steps.description:
Type a backslash and a name, then a space: \all gives ∀, \ex ∃, \to ⇒, \le ≤, \in ∈. The file keeps ASCII escapes like \<forall>; only the editor shows glyphs. Hover a symbol to see how to type it.
[Show Me](command:isabelle.openTutorial?%5B%22symbols%22%5D)
[Symbols Panel](command:isabelle-symbols.focus)

media.altText: A theory with rendered symbols and highlighting; the symbol at the cursor shows its ASCII escape

steps.title: Follow the proof
steps.description:
The Isabelle Infoview in the bottom panel shows the goals and messages at the cursor. Move through a proof and watch the goals change.
[Show Me](command:isabelle.openTutorial?%5B%22goals%22%5D)
[Show Infoview](command:isabelle.infoview)

steps.title: Let Isabelle find proofs
steps.description:
Put the cursor on a sorry and run Sledgehammer. It searches the library and offers proofs to click in.
[Show Me](command:isabelle.openTutorial?%5B%22sledgehammer%22%5D)
[Run Sledgehammer](command:isabelle.sledgehammer)

steps.title: Make it yours
steps.description:
Colours, how far Isabelle checks, how symbols look and type.
[Isabelle Settings](command:toSide:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22%40ext%3Ayfprojects.vscode-isabelle%22%5D)

steps.title: Work on a project
steps.description:
In a folder with a ROOT file, pick the session you work in. Its imports then load from a prebuilt image instead of being checked on every start.
[Select Session Image](command:isabelle.selectTutorialSession)

isabelle.autoStart.description: Start the language server when a theory is open. Turn this off to open .thy files without a prover -- symbol rendering, the outline and symbol input all work without one, and starting a session loads a heap image, which takes a while. Use "Isabelle: Start / Restart Language Server" when you want it.

isabelle.checkWholeTheory.markdownDescription: Check every visible theory to its end. Off, the prover checks each theory from the top down to `vscode_caret_perspective` lines below the cursor (50 unless set in `#isabelle.serverOptions#`) and stops there. Checking is continuous either way; this only sets how far it goes. Takes effect on server restart.

isabelle.completion.inlineSkeletons.markdownDescription: On the blank line below `proof (induct xs)`, `proof (cases x)` and the like, show the proof outline Isabelle prints for it (`case Nil … next case (Cons a xs) … qed`) as ghost text; `Tab` accepts it. With `#isabelle.extendedServer#`, also the definitions and instance proof an `instantiation` still lacks. The same skeletons are always offered from the light bulb, together with those that are only suggestions (an Isar sketch of a goal, subgoal blocks).

isabelle.continuousChecking.description: Deprecated name of isabelle.checkWholeTheory, still read when that one is not set.
isabelle.continuousChecking.markdownDeprecationMessage: Renamed to `#isabelle.checkWholeTheory#`: the prover checks continuously either way, and the setting only decides how far down a theory it goes. This name is still read when the new one is not set.

isabelle.expandAbbreviations.markdownDescription: Expand `\forall` into `\<forall>` as you type, and the short forms such as `\all`, `\ne`, `\iff`, `\_1` or `\[[` (caret inside `\<lbrakk>…\<rbrakk>`). Hover a symbol to see every way to type it.

isabelle.extendedServer.markdownDescription: Start Isabelle's language server with the additions this extension ships: the Query, Theories, Timing, Simplifier Trace and Graph View panels, Go to Command, and session images for `-R` that build. Your Isabelle installation is not modified. Available for Isabelle2025-2. Takes effect after reloading the window.

isabelle.input.customShorthands.markdownDescription: Your own `\` shorthands, added to the built-in ones and overriding them: `{"cup": "∪", "pair": "\\<langle>$CURSOR\\<rangle>"}` makes `\cup` type `\<union>`. Write the symbol as a glyph or as `\<name>`; the file always gets the ASCII escape. `$CURSOR` marks where the caret goes.

isabelle.graphview.description: Show the Graph View panel, which draws the output of thy_deps, class_deps, locale_deps and code_deps. The PIDE/graphview_* messages exist only on the vscode-graphview branch of mirror-isabelle.

isabelle.home.markdownDescription: Path to the Isabelle distribution (the directory containing `bin/isabelle`). Empty: use `$ISABELLE_HOME`, then well-known install locations.

isabelle.logic.description: Session image the language server boots with (isabelle vscode_server -l/-R). Imports already in this image load from a heap and are never re-checked; every other theory is elaborated from source on each start. The default "HOL" caches no project theory. Use "Isabelle: Select Session Image" to pick one from the ROOT files in the workspace.

isabelle.logicRequirements.markdownDescription: Start from an image built of `#isabelle.logic#`'s **requirements** (`-R`) rather than the session itself (`-l`). Use this when the theories you are editing belong to that session: everything they import is then loaded from a prebuilt heap and is never re-checked, while your own files stay live.
isabelle.logicRequirements.description: Boot with the chosen session's *requirements* (-R) rather than the session itself (-l). This is what you want while editing that session: everything it imports comes from a heap, while its own theories stay live and editable. With -l the session's own theories are in the image too, so they are not checked at all.

enumDescriptions: Colour checked text from the active colour theme, by serving PIDE markup as semantic tokens. Installing a theme then recolours the whole file.
Colour checked text from Isabelle's own text_color palette, as Isabelle/jEdit and the official Isabelle/VSCode do. The theme will not affect checked text.
isabelle.markupColors.markdownDescription: Who colours text that PIDE has checked. Processing status, message underlines and overview marks are unaffected either way. Note that `theme` relies on semantic highlighting, which `#editor.semanticHighlighting.enabled#` leaves to the theme by default; a theme that opts out falls back to the TextMate grammar.

isabelle.normalizeOnSave.markdownDescription: Before saving, rewrite any literal Unicode symbols back to `\<name>` escapes. `isabelle build` rejects literal Unicode, so this keeps files loadable.

isabelle.pideMarkup.markdownDescription: Apply PIDE markup (syntax colouring and processing status) as editor decorations.

isabelle.pideViewportScope.markdownDescription: Apply PIDE markup only to the visible part of the document (plus `#isabelle.renderMarginLines#`). The server sends markup for the whole file - over 51000 ranges on a 9000-line theory - and applying all of it costs roughly 40ms per keystroke. Disable only to compare against that behaviour.

isabelle.queryPanel.markdownDescription: Show the Query panel (find_theorems / find_consts). Requires an Isabelle whose language server exposes the `PIDE/query_*` messages; released versions do not. See the `vscode-query-panel` branch of mirror-isabelle.

isabelle.renderMarginLines.markdownDescription: How many lines above and below the viewport to decorate. Cost is linear in decorated ranges; keep the resulting count well under ~1500.

isabelle.renderSymbols.markdownDescription: Render `\<forall>`-style symbol escapes as Unicode glyphs using editor decorations. The file on disk stays ASCII.

isabelle.revealSymbolAtCursor.markdownDescription: Show the raw `\<name>` escape instead of the glyph for the symbol the cursor is inside, so it can be edited.

isabelle.serverArgs.description: Additional raw arguments appended to isabelle vscode_server.

isabelle.serverOptions.markdownDescription:
Isabelle system options passed as `-o NAME=VALUE`.

`vscode_pide_extensions` enables PIDE markup decorations and the infoview. `vscode_html_output` makes the infoview receive HTML, and also avoids an Isabelle2025-2 bug where the non-HTML branch fails to serialise decorations. `vscode_unicode_symbols_output` renders glyphs in panels and hovers.

Do **not** enable `vscode_unicode_symbols_edits`: those edits are inserted into the buffer, which must stay ASCII.

isabelle.sledgehammer.maxParallel.markdownDescription: How many Sledgehammer runs go at once; more wait their turn. Each run keeps several external provers busy, so more than the cores can carry makes every run slower. Needs `#isabelle.extendedServer#`, like the settings below: without it there is one run at a time, and it ends when its command is edited.

isabelle.sledgehammer.stopAtFirstProof.markdownDescription: End a Sledgehammer run at its first proof (`max_proofs = 1`), instead of looking for up to four, so that the provers go to the next run. The panel's checkbox overrides this for the window.

isabelle.sledgehammer.timeout.description: Seconds each Sledgehammer run may take. The panel's field overrides this for the window.

isabelle.sledgehammer.falsify.markdownDescription: Let Sledgehammer also look for a *falsification* (`falsify = smart`): facts that the goal contradicts. A step that is false then says so early, instead of running into the timeout with no proof. The panel's checkbox overrides this for the window.

isabelle.sledgehammer.cache.markdownDescription: Keep the answers of the external provers (Sledgehammer's `cache_dir`, in the extension's storage), so that a goal hammered again, after an edit above it or a restart, is answered without running them. **Isabelle: Clear Sledgehammer Cache** empties it.

isabelle.sledgehammer.autoSorry.markdownDescription: Run Sledgehammer on every `sorry` in view that has had no run yet, a moment after typing stops. Each one then gets a CodeLens with the proof found. Off by default: it keeps the provers busy. **Isabelle: Sledgehammer All sorrys** does the same for one lemma on request.

isabelle.simplifierTrace.description: Show the Simplifier Trace panel. The PIDE/simplifier_trace_* messages exist only on the vscode-simplifier-trace branch of mirror-isabelle, so against a stock distribution this view would stay empty. Enable tracing with `declare [[simp_trace_new interactive mode=full]]` before the simp call, or `using [[simp_trace_new interactive mode=full]]` on the simp call itself.

isabelle.spellChecker.markdownDescription: Use Isabelle's own spell checker, which checks prose in comments and `text ‹…›` blocks by PIDE markup category (so antiquotations inside prose are excluded). General spell-checking extensions such as Code Spell Checker cannot tell prose from formulas here: VS Code does not expose TextMate scopes to extensions, so they see the whole theory as plain text (and Code Spell Checker skips the `isabelle` file type unless enabled). Turn this off only if you check spelling some other way.

isabelle.textColorOverrides.markdownDescription: Override individual PIDE markup colours, keyed `<name>_light` / `<name>_dark` (e.g. `keyword1_dark`). Defaults come from Isabelle's own palette.

isabelle.theoriesPanel.description: Show the Theories and Timing views. Requires the vscode-theories-panel branch of mirror-isabelle; a released Isabelle does not answer PIDE/theories_request.

isabelle.timingThreshold.description: Timing view: only commands at or above this many seconds are reported.

isabelle.agents.enabled.markdownDescription: Offer the prover of this window to AI agents (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, any MCP client) as tools: check a theory, show the goals at a line, try proof candidates and Sledgehammer without editing the file, find theorems. Served only on this machine (127.0.0.1) and only to agents holding the token in `~/.isabelle-vscode/agents`. **Isabelle: Set Up AI Agents** turns this on and adds the server to a project's `.mcp.json`. Needs the extended server (`#isabelle.extendedServer#`). See [AI agents](https://github.com/real-yfprojects/vscode-isabelle/blob/main/docs/agents.md).

semanticTokenTypes.description: Isabelle command (lemma, definition, have, by, qed)
Isabelle minor keyword (where, and, fixes, shows) and `end`
Isabelle proof command that fixes, assumes or states a goal (fix, assume, obtain, case, show, thus)
Isabelle improper command (apply, done, prefer, defer)
Isabelle constant (a logical constant such as `map` or `Suc`)
